---
title: "Simulation (paper), step 5: estimates of the Bayesian models"
---

Step 5 of the paper simulation (ML design): point estimates (median) and 95 % quantile intervals (QI)
of recall, precision and F1 from every fit of step 4. The comparison with the truths follows in the
evaluation (step 7 and `S3_Code_Simulation_Coverage.Rmd`).

**Estimand:** marginal pooled and grouped value of the superpopulation of slides.

- Per posterior draw the estimated recall and precision of every observed slide (with its fitted
  slide effect; `re_formula = NULL`), expected counts E[TP] = P · recall, E[FP] = E[TP] ·
  (1 − precision) / precision.
- Bayesian bootstrap: Dirichlet(1, …, 1) weights over the slides (`rexp()`), new for every draw.
  - pooled: weighted sums of the expected counts;
  - grouped: weighted mean of the per-slide metrics.
- Draws: all 4000 saved draws.

**Seed** (offset from `01_seed_offsets.csv`)

- `seed + 3000000` per fit: Dirichlet weights.
- The mirai daemons use the L'Ecuyer-CMRG random number generator (not R's default
  Mersenne-Twister); in a normal R session, set `RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG")` first.

**Run**

- Parallel with `purrr::map()` and `in_parallel()` on mirai daemons (11 workers). The functions
  are placed on the daemons with `mirai::everywhere()`.
- One file per fit. Fits whose estimates file exists are skipped, so the step can be restarted and
  run while step 4 is still fitting (only existing fits are used).

**Output** (`simulation/estimates/`)

- `<model_id>/<scenario>_<n_slide>_v<variant>_r<rep>.csv`: estimates of one fit.
- `05_bayes_estimates.csv.xz`: all estimates combined: `scenario`, `n_slide`, `rep`, `variant`,
  `model`, `model_id`, `estimand`, `averaging`, `name`, `interval`, `value`, `.lower`, `.upper`.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
```

# Functions
```{r}
# F1-score from the counts (paper eq. 3); defined if TP = 0 (paper "Case B": 0)
calc_F1_score <- function(TP, FP, P) {
  2 * TP / (P + TP + FP)
}

# Columns for the binomial + Poisson model and the multinomial model (as in step 3)
prepare_brms_data <- function(df_sim) {
  df_sim |>
    mutate(
      # Binomial + Poisson
      GroundTruth = TP + FN,    # Sensitivity/recall trials: all true objects (P)
      # Multinomial
      N = TP + FN + FP,         # trials: all counted cells
      Y = cbind(TP = TP, FN = FN, FP = FP),
      # Object density, centred on the mean of log(P)
      P_log = as.numeric(scale(log(P), center = TRUE, scale = FALSE))
    )
}

# Per posterior draw: recall and precision of every observed slide (fitted slide effects).
# The trials are set to 1, so .epred are probabilities (or the FP count):
#   multinomial:        cell probabilities of TP, FN, FP
#                       -> recall = TP / (TP + FN), precision = TP / (TP + FP)
#   binomial + Poisson: recall (TP) and expected FP count of the slide (FP)
#                       -> precision = recall * P / (recall * P + FP)
epred_recall_precision <- function(fit, df_sim) {
  newdata <- prepare_brms_data(df_sim) |>
    select(slide, P, P_log) |>
    mutate(GroundTruth = 1, N = 1)

  df_draws <- epred_draws(fit, newdata = newdata, re_formula = NULL) |>
    ungroup() |>
    select(.draw, slide, P, .category, .epred) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = .category, values_from = .epred)

  if ("FN" %in% names(df_draws)) { # Multinomial
    df_draws |>
      mutate(Recall = TP / (TP + FN), Precision = TP / (TP + FP)) |>
      select(-TP, -FN, -FP)
  } else {                         # Binomial + Poisson
    df_draws |>
      mutate(Recall = TP, Precision = TP * P / (TP * P + FP)) |>
      select(-TP, -FP)
  }
}

# Marginal estimate (model + Bayesian bootstrap): per posterior draw the expected counts of each
# observed slide, averaged with Dirichlet(1, ..., 1) weights over the slides (new for every draw)
#   pooled  = weighted sums of the expected counts
#   grouped = weighted mean of the per-slide metrics
bayes_marginal_metrics <- function(fit, df_sim) {
  epred_recall_precision(fit, df_sim) |>
    mutate(
      TP = Recall * P,
      FP = TP * (1 - Precision) / Precision
    ) |>
    group_by(.draw) |>
    mutate(weight = rexp(n())) |>
    summarise(
      Recall_pooled     = sum(weight * TP) / sum(weight * P),
      Precision_pooled  = sum(weight * TP) / sum(weight * (TP + FP)),
      F1_pooled         = calc_F1_score(sum(weight * TP), sum(weight * FP), sum(weight * P)),
      Recall_grouped    = weighted.mean(Recall, weight),
      Precision_grouped = weighted.mean(Precision, weight),
      F1_grouped        = weighted.mean(calc_F1_score(TP, FP, P), weight)
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(matches("_(pooled|grouped)$"),
                 names_to = c("name", "averaging"), names_sep = "_") |>
    group_by(name, averaging) |>
    median_qi(value) |>
    transmute(estimand = "marginal", averaging, name, interval = "qi", value, .lower, .upper)
}
```

# Settings
```{r}
n_workers     <- 11
dir_fits      <- "simulation/fits"
dir_estimates <- "simulation/estimates"

# Short model ids for the file names (as in step 4)
df_models <- tribble(
  ~model,              ~model_id,
  "Binomial + Poisson", "binomial_poisson",
  "Multinomial",        "multinomial"
)
```

# Load data
```{r}
df_seed_offsets <- read_csv("simulation/data/01_seed_offsets.csv")
df_counts       <- read_csv("simulation/data/02_ML_performance_observed_data.csv.xz")

offset_bayes <- df_seed_offsets |> filter(step == "bayes_postprocessing") |> pull(offset)
```

# Jobs
```{r}
df_jobs <- df_counts |>
  nest(data = c(slide, P, TP, FN, FP)) |>
  mutate(seed_bayes = seed + offset_bayes) |>
  cross_join(df_models) |>
  mutate(
    file_name      = sprintf("%s_%d_v%d_r%03d", scenario, n_slide, variant, rep),
    file_fit       = file.path(dir_fits, model_id, paste0(file_name, ".rds")),
    file_estimates = file.path(dir_estimates, model_id, paste0(file_name, ".csv"))
  ) |>
  # only existing fits without estimates
  filter(file.exists(file_fit), !file.exists(file_estimates)) |>
  arrange(rep, scenario, n_slide, variant, model_id)

nrow(df_jobs)
```

# Estimates
```{r}
walk(file.path(dir_estimates, df_models$model_id), \(dir) dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE))

mirai::daemons(n_workers)
invisible(mirai::everywhere(
  {
    setwd(dir_project)
    library(dplyr)
    library(tidyr)
    library(readr)
    library(brms)
    library(tidybayes)
  },
  dir_project = getwd(),
  calc_F1_score = calc_F1_score, prepare_brms_data = prepare_brms_data,
  epred_recall_precision = epred_recall_precision, bayes_marginal_metrics = bayes_marginal_metrics
))

t_start <- Sys.time()
df_errors <- df_jobs |>
  split(seq_len(nrow(df_jobs))) |>
  map(in_parallel(\(job) {
    tryCatch({
      fit <- readRDS(job$file_fit)

      set.seed(job$seed_bayes)
      bayes_marginal_metrics(fit, job$data[[1]]) |>
        mutate(scenario = job$scenario, n_slide = job$n_slide, rep = job$rep, variant = job$variant,
               model = job$model, model_id = job$model_id) |>
        select(scenario, n_slide, rep, variant, model, model_id, estimand, averaging, name,
               interval, value, .lower, .upper) |>
        write_csv(job$file_estimates)
      NULL
    }, error = \(e) tibble(file_fit = job$file_fit, error = conditionMessage(e)))
  }), .progress = TRUE) |>
  bind_rows()
mirai::daemons(0)

difftime(Sys.time(), t_start, units = "hours")

# Failed fits (no estimates file, retried in the next run)
df_errors
```

# Combine
```{r}
# Only the per-fit files in the model folders
df_bayes_estimates <- list.files(file.path(dir_estimates, df_models$model_id), pattern = "\\.csv$",
                                 full.names = TRUE) |>
  read_csv()
write_csv(df_bayes_estimates, file.path(dir_estimates, "05_bayes_estimates.csv.xz"))

# Number of estimated fits per model, scenario and variant
df_bayes_estimates |>
  distinct(model, scenario, variant, n_slide, rep) |>
  count(model, scenario, variant, name = "fits")
```
